prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a hit while turning left in Sugar Land, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1382; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but I can confirm I'm the driver of the vehicle involved.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where the accident happened?
A: It was at an intersection in Sugar Land, Texas. I was turning left across the lanes to get into a shopping center parking lot.
Q: What were the traffic conditions when you started your turn?
A: It was fairly light. I checked for oncoming cars, and I saw one a fair distance away, so I started to go.
Q: What happened next?
A: A vehicle coming from the opposite direction hit the front passenger side of my car. I think they were going faster than the speed limit, but I can't be sure.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?
A: Not clearly. I glanced back at the road and then there was a loud bang and my car spun a little.
Q: Were you injured?
A: Yes. My neck snapped forward and then back, and I have pain in my neck and upper back. I also have headaches that started later that day.
Q: Did you seek medical attention?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic that evening. They took X-rays and told me it looked like whiplash. I've been referred to a physical therapist.
Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?
A: Yes. Turning my head to the right is hard, and sitting for long periods makes it worse.
Q: Did you make any statements at the scene to the other driver or police?
A: I told the officer I was okay at first, because I didn't realize how stiff I'd become. I did tell him what I remembered about the turn.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything you'd like to add?
A: Only that I'm still getting treatment, and I'm keeping copies of all my medical bills.
Q: Thank you for your time. This concludes the statement.
